market_context_2026_08.vn_index_note: +0.82% on Aug-04, outperforming the rest of Asia that session. The index has run into the upgrade, not away from it.
market_context_2026_08.estimated_passive_inflow_usd: several billion; a commonly cited figure is ~USD 6bn
market_context_2026_08.inflow_confidence: LOW — this number is repeated across secondary sources without a consistent methodology. Treat it as a direction, not a quantity.
market_context_2026_08.front_running_read: A confirmed, dated, ten-month-telegraphed index event is the most efficiently front-run category of catalyst that exists. Passive funds are price-insensitive buyers on a known date, which is precisely why active money arrives first.

routes.label: Thai-domiciled Vietnam equity feeder fund (settles in THB)
routes.confidence: LOW — generic placeholder fee assumptions (~1.9% stacked TER, 1% front load). Pull an actual fund factsheet/FCT before relying on this line.
routes.advantages: No offshore account, no THB->USD spread paid directly, no US estate-tax situs, simpler Thai tax treatment.
routes.disadvantages: Fees stack: the Thai feeder charges on top of the master fund. FX exposure is not removed, only hidden inside the NAV.

routes.label: VanEck Vietnam ETF (VNM, NYSE Arca) via a Thai offshore account
routes.confidence: medium — TER ~0.66-0.68% and AUM ~USD 560-640m are well sourced; the broker tariff (0.25% / USD 15 minimum) is a representative placeholder.
flags: COMMISSION MINIMUM BINDING — a USD 15 floor on a ~USD 897 ticket is 1.67%, not 0.25%. This is the single most avoidable cost in the whole analysis and it is caused entirely by the small position size.

US ESTATE-TAX SITUS — US-listed securities held by a non-resident alien carry only a USD 60,000 exemption. Not binding today (the whole book is ~USD 18k) but it constrains how large an offshore sleeve can sensibly get.
Small fund AUM means bid/ask and premium/discount to NAV are a real secondary cost not captured above.

cost_analysis.headline_finding: Both routes cost roughly 11-12% of the position over a 24-month medium-term hold BEFORE the market does anything. That is not a rounding error — it is the entire realistic return of a diversifying satellite position.
cost_analysis.largest_single_cost_both_routes: VND structural currency drift (~6% over 24 months)
cost_analysis.why_that_matters: The State Bank of Vietnam runs a managed crawling band that has depreciated the dong against the USD in most years, ~2-4%/yr. For a THB-based investor this stacks BEHIND the THB/USD leg. Unlike volatility it is not two-sided — it is a near-certain negative carry, and it is larger than the TER on either route. Almost no retail write-up on the FTSE upgrade mentions it.

size_sensitivity.note: Raising the position reduces cost only slowly, because the dominant cost is the currency drift, which is size-invariant.
size_sensitivity.read: Even TRIPLING the position to an uncomfortable 15% of the ex-gold book only takes the cheapest route from 10.8% to 9.8%. There is no size at which this becomes cheap.

diversification_assessment.the_actual_problem: The ex-gold book is 100% single-country Thai equity, and on the 2026-08-05 snapshot all three positions sit at or above the 30% concentration flag (SCB 35.7%, PTTEP 34.2%, BAFS 30.1%).
diversification_assessment.does_vietnam_fix_it: Weakly. Vietnam and Thailand are both ASEAN economies levered to the same underlying factors — export manufacturing, China demand, regional tourism, USD funding conditions and the oil complex. Swapping single-country Thai concentration for two-country ASEAN concentration is a modest improvement, not a solution.
diversification_assessment.correlation_caveat: No correlation study was run for this file. The claim above is structural reasoning, not a measured statistic — treat it as a hypothesis worth testing before it is relied on.
cheaper_alternatives_for_the_same_goal: The EXISTING SCBGOLDE sleeve already provides genuine non-Thai, non-equity diversification at a 0.50% TER, settles in THB, and needs no new account. It is roughly a tenth the annual cost of either Vietnam route.
A broad EM or global equity fund diversifies the single-country risk far more than a single frontier-to-EM market does, and typically at a lower TER than a country feeder fund.
Simply trimming the largest Thai position reduces concentration at SET commission cost only, with no FX leg at all.

decision.verdict: DO NOT open a Vietnam position for the FTSE catalyst.
decision.primary_reason: The all-in cost of ~11-12% over the intended 24-month hold consumes the entire plausible return of a satellite diversifier, and the dominant cost line (VND drift) cannot be engineered away by better execution or better sizing.
decision.secondary_reason: The catalyst has been public since October 2025 and the VN-Index has already run into it. Buying a price-insensitive, known-date passive flow ten months after it was announced is the crowded side of the trade.
decision.tertiary_reason: Even if it worked, it is the wrong instrument for the problem it is being proposed to solve. The concentration issue is 100%-Thailand, and Vietnam is a correlated ASEAN neighbour.
what_would_change_this: A verified THB-settled Vietnam vehicle with a real TER below ~1.0% and no front load — that alone removes ~3 points of cost.
An intended position size above ~THB 150,000, which makes the fixed commission floor irrelevant (though the VND drift persists).
A material post-Sep-21 give-back in the VN-Index, which would convert this from a catalyst trade into a valuation one — a much better reason to own something.
Evidence that VND drift has structurally stopped, which would remove the largest single cost line.
decision.explicitly_not_claimed: This is not a view that Vietnam is a bad economy or a bad long-term market. It is a view that Tho cannot access it cheaply enough, at the size he would sensibly use, for this particular catalyst to be worth it.
decision.advisory_note_for_tho: The useful takeaway here is not about Vietnam. It is that any new foreign position at your current book size carries a fixed-cost floor that quietly eats a diversifier's whole return, and that managed-float currencies add a second charge nobody advertises. Before the next international idea arrives, the cheaper first move is fixing the concentration you already have inside markets you already pay to access. I am not a licensed financial adviser and this is analysis, not a recommendation to buy or sell — the fee and tax figures in particular are estimates that should be confirmed with your broker and fund documents.
